previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and chest pressure following her recent bilateral nephrectomy. She was found to be in atrial flutter with a rapid ventricular rate, and imaging revealed new bilateral pleural effusions and possible pericardial effusion. An echocardiogram showed a reduced ejection fraction of 29%, consistent with acute on chronic systolic heart failure, likely exacerbated by tachycardia. She underwent hemodialysis with ultrafiltration, resulting in significant symptom improvement. A transesophageal echocardiogram ruled out intracardiac clots, and successful cardioversion restored sinus rhythm. Her warfarin dose was adjusted due to a subtherapeutic INR on admission, and she was transitioned from atenolol to metoprolol for better rate control. Amlodipine was discontinued due to well-controlled blood pressure. She remained afebrile without diarrhea, and her C. diff treatment was continued. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged for cardiology and infectious disease.

Calcium-9.2 Phos-4.7* Mg-2.___ year-old female with PCKD status-post bilateral nephrectomy 
on HD, hypertension, PAF on coumadin, mild systolic dysfunction, 
moderate MR/TR admitted with shortness of breath x2 days. Brief 
hospital course was as follows.

1. Decompensated systolic heart failure:  Shortness of breath 
was likely due to decompensated heart failure secondary to 
multiple pathologies, including paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, 
mitral regurgitation, decreased LV systolic function, and fluid 
overload due to missed dialysis session. With 3+ MR and 
decreased systolic function (EF 45%), suspect that atrial 
fibrillation with RVR may be the tipping point with decreased 
forward flow and resultant congestive heart failure. Further 
complicated during this hospitalization due to inability to have 
dialysis per usual regimen on ___ (___). Given 
presence of chest pressure at times, initially ACS also in the 
differential - although unlikely given that troponin lower than 
baseline, and EKG without ischemic changes. Patient did not 
experience dyspnea during hospital course, at rest or with 
exertion. She remained in sinus rhythm throughout. Intermittent 
chest pressure resolved after large-volume dialysis. Regarding 
systolic heart failure, patient should be started on ACE 
inhibitor as outpatient.

2. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation:  Sinus rhythm for duration of 
hospital course. Continued amiodarone per home regimen. 
Beta-blocker reduced from metoprolol tartrate 50mg PO BID to 
37.5mg PO BID given bradycardia and lightheadedness. Coumadin 
held throughout hospital course given supratherapeutic INR, with 
plan for recheck within 24 hours of discharge.

3. Mitral regurgitation:  Moderate to severe. Given LV 
dilatation, unclear if patient is candidate for MVR. Concern 
expressed with primary cardiologist, and further management on 
outpatient basis at this time.

4. Hyperkalemia:  On admission. Likely secondary to requiring 
HD. Without EKG changes. Received calcium gluconate, insulin, 
and D50 in the emergency department. Potassium normalized after 
hemodialysis.

5. Polycystic kidney disease s/p bilateral nephrectomy:  HD MWF. 
Missed ___ session due to holiday. Continued Sevelamer per 
home regimen.

6. Hypertension:  For unclear reason, patient was started on 
midodrine several years ago. She is working with her 
cardiologist at present to slowly reduce dose. Beta-blocker dose 
was decreased, as above. Given systolic heart failure, ACE 
inhibitor should be started on outpatient basis.

7. Anemia:  Remained at baseline. Receives iron IV, Epogen at 
dialysis.

8. Hypothyroidism:  Continued levothyroxine per home regimen. 
TSH checked and within normal limits.
